ai.headline: OpenAI's WebRTC split-relay architecture for 900M weekly voice AI users
ai.body: OpenAI decoupled packet routing from protocol termination: a stateless relay at the geographic edge reads the ICE ufrag field as a routing key and forwards encrypted media to the correct stateful transceiver without decrypting or modifying it. The transceiver owns all heavy WebRTC state — ICE, DTLS handshake, SRTP keys — and is pinned to a single process, solving Kubernetes port-exhaustion and state-stickiness problems simultaneously. They deliberately rejected SFU architecture (suited for multiparty) and TURN (extra round-trip latency) in favour of this custom relay/transceiver split built on Pion (Go), SO_REUSEPORT, thread pinning, and a Redis-backed flow table for restart recovery.

swe.headline: ICE ufrag as a zero-overhead routing key: lessons for stateful-service/stateless-proxy splits in Kubernetes
swe.body: The core engineering insight is embedding transceiver routing metadata inside an existing protocol field (ICE ufrag) that the client already sends on the first packet, eliminating any database round-trip from the hot path. The relay remains effectively stateless — its in-memory flow table is reconstructable from the ufrag after a restart — which enables independent scaling and rolling deploys without session affinity hacks at the load balancer. The tradeoff is full ownership of signaling: the technique requires controlling server-side ufrag generation, making it incompatible with off-the-shelf signaling stacks.

deepDives.why: Primary source engineering post from OpenAI's infrastructure team detailing the relay/transceiver architecture, ufrag routing trick, and Kubernetes deployment constraints at 900M weekly user scale — directly applicable to any team building real-time audio or stateful-service/stateless-proxy systems on Kubernetes.
